item.text: The campaign is live, and X accepted all four approved posts. It is scheduled to stop at midnight Arizona time after February 15, with combined lifetime caps of $650. I’ll check delivery and cost per completed entry, then move budget toward the stronger posts as results accumulate.
All four posts are delivering. Reporting shows $42.15 spent and one attributed entry so far. That is too little conversion data to pick a winner, so I’ll keep the test balanced for now.

The first day shows three attributed entries on $126.25 of reported spend. The deadline post has two entries and the couch-inheritance post has one. Click-through is low across the test, so I’ll narrow delivery to people interested in pets while keeping the US and 21+ requirements.

Reporting now shows six attributed entries on $174.94 spent. The deadline post leads with three entries at about $14.61 each; the other posts have one each at about $44. I’ll give the deadline post more budget while continuing to test the others.

At the end of Friday, reported spend is $254.58 with eight attributed entries. The deadline post still has the lowest cost per entry, followed by the eligibility post. I’ll keep the current allocation through the next check.

The couch-inheritance and eligibility posts have caught up on efficiency: each now has three entries at about $23.39 per entry, close to the deadline post’s $24.54. Total reported entries are 11 on $289.99 spent. I’ll keep all three in rotation and continue limiting the homepage-invitation post.

Going into Super Bowl Sunday, X reports 15 entries on $387.55 spent. The eligibility post is now strongest at about $18.42 per entry. I’ll pause the homepage-invitation post, which still has one attributed entry after $62.23 spent, and shift more budget to the eligibility post while retaining the deadline and humor posts.

Sunday’s midday check shows 16 attributed entries and $427.29 spent. The eligibility post continues to lead on cost per entry. The three active groups are delivering, with $222.71 remaining under the overall budget.

The eligibility post brought in five more reported entries overnight, reaching 11 at about $13.43 each. Total campaign results are 22 attributed entries on $511.06 spent. For the final day, I’ll pause the humor post and give the eligibility post more of the remaining budget, alongside the deadline post.
Monday’s midday report is $548.69 spent, with entries still at 22. The two remaining posts are delivering within their caps. I’ll check again this evening before the scheduled midnight stop.

With six hours left in the flight, X reports $583.42 spent, 360,312 impressions and 198 link clicks. Attributed entries remain at 22. I’ll let the two selected posts finish within their caps, then verify the campaign has stopped.

The flight has ended at midnight Arizona time. The campaign is expired and paused, and X confirms it cannot serve. I’ll pull the latest available reporting for the recap; the most recent activity may still be processing.

Couch Captain’s February 11–15 Arizona flight has ended, and the campaign is stopped.

- Spend: **$645.07** of $650
- Impressions: **389,992**
- Link clicks: **215**
- Attributed completed entries: **28**
- Cost per attributed entry: **$23.04**

I used only your approved posts and shifted budget toward stronger entry performance. These are X’s latest reported totals; late reporting may adjust them.
